caption:
A SpaceX Falcon 9 booster reaches space, separates from its payload, then flips around and lands itself back on the pad.

Before SpaceX cracked this, every rocket was thrown away after a single use. Now these boosters land, get inspected, and fly again, sometimes within weeks. The one in this clip has almost certainly launched more than once.

That switch from disposable to reusable cut the cost of reaching orbit by more than half, and it's the reason a rocket launch has gone from a rare event to something that happens roughly every few days.
